newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Light plans 6.7 pct rate rise - paper.
newsitem.headline: China Light plans 6.7 pct rate rise - paper.

text.p: China Light & Power Co has applied for a 6.7 percent increase in electricity tariffs, a Hong Kong newspaper reported on Saturday.
The Hong Kong government confirmed its energy advisory committee held a meeting on Friday to consider China Light's application.
But in a statement, the government denied the report in the Chinese-language Ming Pao newspaper that it had approved the rate rise, which would come into effect in March.
China Light also raised electricity rates by an average of 6.7 percent last March.

Last week the power utility sold 20 percent of its enlarged share capital to CITIC Pacific, the Hong Kong-listed arm of China's state trading giant China International Trust and Investment Corp, at HK$32.66 per share.
Analysts said the link with the powerful mainland firm would enable China Light to expand into the Chinese market.
